feedback:
The candidate's rationale says to move the sensors from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07 m, but the geometry still has every sensor at y = 0.05 m. As written, it is identical to iteration 6, the best raced design (score 570.4). Racing it would retest iteration 6 and not test the look-ahead hypothesis. Revise the geometry so all five sensors sit at y = 0.07 m, keeping x at -0.04 to 0.04 m in 0.02 m steps, sensor_size 0.016, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.3, mass 0.6 kg and last_direction line loss unchanged, so the single change is isolated.

The evidence behind the change is iteration 6. Moving the sensors from y 0.03 to 0.05 raised oval completion to 20 of 20 and s-bend completion to 9 of 20, and it lifted slalom progress from 0.28 to 0.41, though slalom still finished 0 of 20 at max_error near the 0.06 m limit. Expected from the forward look-ahead: slalom and s-bend max_error should fall and slalom progress should rise. The oval should stay near full completion. Nothing here predicts the outcome of the revised build, which has not raced.

After the next race, read the results in this order. (a) If oval completion falls below 20 of 20 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, the forward lead is overshooting on straights or amplifying jitter, so return y to 0.06 and, if needed, lower kd toward 0.6. (b) If the slalom still exits at max_error near 0.06 with no gain from y, steering authority is the limit, so raise kp to about 3.3 with kd held. (c) If progress stalls below 0.3 on the s-bend with no off-track exit, base_speed is too low for the 3 s limit, so raise it toward 1.4 in 0.1 steps.
requested_changes: Set every sensor's y to 0.07 m (sensor_positions y = 0.07 for all five entries), keeping x at -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 m and sensor_size 0.016. The current build still has y = 0.05 m, so it matches iteration 6 and does not test the change; iteration 6 showed y 0.03 to 0.05 raised oval completion to 20 of 20 and slalom progress to 0.41.

If, after the race, oval completion drops below 20 of 20 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, return sensor y to 0.06 m, since iteration 6 showed the forward lead is the lever that works and the oval was at full completion there.

If the slalom still exits off track at max_error near 0.06 m with no gain in progress from y 0.07, raise kp from 3.0 toward 3.3 with kd held at 0.8, since iteration 4 showed kp 3.7 hurt the harder tracks at y 0.03 and steering authority is the remaining limit.
